nextjs.recommended_path: Vercel — native runtime. Push to a linked Git repo and Vercel builds + deploys automatically. App Router, ISR, Edge runtime, Image Optimization, Server Actions, RSC all first-class.
caveats: Hobby plan caps function execution at 10s; Pro extends to 60s, Enterprise to 15m.
Image Optimization volume bills separately above plan-included free tier.
Serverless function bundle limit ~50MB unzipped — sharp / canvas / large native deps eat the budget fast.

astro.recommended_path: Vercel with @astrojs/vercel adapter (serverless or edge). Static + hybrid + server modes all supported.
caveats: Pick the serverless adapter unless you specifically need the edge runtime; edge has a smaller stdlib.
Astro DB (libSQL) is separate from Vercel Postgres — pick one path.

sveltekit.recommended_path: Vercel with @sveltejs/adapter-vercel. Hands-off setup; the adapter auto-detects Vercel features.
caveats: form actions are POST-heavy — wire a rate-limit at edge middleware or upstream.

remix.recommended_path: Vercel via @vercel/remix or the Remix Vite + Vercel template. Loaders/actions become serverless or edge functions automatically.
caveats: Long-running side-effects in actions need to move to a queue (Vercel Cron + DB job table or Inngest).

nuxt.recommended_path: Vercel with `nuxt build --preset=vercel` (or `vercel-edge`). Nitro engine handles the abstraction.
caveats: Verify any Nitro modules used are edge-compatible if you pick the edge preset.

solidstart.recommended_path: Vercel with the SolidStart Vercel preset. SSR + static both supported.

vite-spa.recommended_path: Vercel — drop the dist/ output as static. Pure SPA, no SSR needed. Vercel's CDN + Image Optimization are still on the table.

vue.recommended_path: Vercel auto-detects Vue 3 + Vite projects. Static build → CDN. For SSR Vue, use Nuxt instead.

hono.recommended_path: Vercel as edge functions: `npm i hono @hono/node-server`, deploy as a single edge handler. Hono's adapter for Vercel is the canonical path.
caveats: Edge runtime stdlib is smaller than Node — verify any imported package is edge-safe.

static-html.recommended_path: Vercel — drop the directory; done. Add `vercel.json` only if custom redirects/headers are needed.

express.recommended_path: API-only Express can be deployed via the `api/` directory pattern (each handler becomes a serverless function), OR wrapped in a single function that mounts Express. Better long-term: rewrite to Hono on edge or move to a long-running host (Fly/Railway/AWS).
caveats: `app.listen()` is a no-op on Vercel — export the Express app as the function handler.
Sessions / cookies in memory don't survive between invocations — move to Vercel KV or Postgres.
Serverless function timeouts cap long requests (10s Hobby / 60s Pro / 15m Enterprise).

fastify.recommended_path: Same as Express. Fastify's plugin model often makes the wrapper more mechanical. Bind `fastify.ready()` then call `fastify.server.emit('request', req, res)` from the function handler.
caveats: fastify-multipart streaming uploads → @vercel/blob multipart upload.

nestjs.recommended_path: NestJS on Vercel via `@vendia/serverless-express`-style wrapper around `NestFactory.create`. Cold starts are heavier; consider Vercel Fluid Compute or move to a long-running host.
caveats: Microservices via TCP/Redis transports won't run on Vercel.
TypeORM/Sequelize over TCP have slow cold starts on serverless — switch to Drizzle + Vercel Postgres pooled connection.

api-only-monorepo.recommended_path: Treat `api/` as the function tree. Put a thin Hono router per file, or one omnibus handler. Avoid framework lock-in if cold-start matters.
caveats: Per-file functions cap at the project's function count limit (varies by plan).

hugo.recommended_path: Vercel with the Hugo build preset. Build command: `hugo --minify`. Output: `public/`.

jekyll.recommended_path: Vercel with the Jekyll build preset. Output: `_site/`.

eleventy.recommended_path: Vercel — output `_site/` or `dist/` depending on config.

gatsby.recommended_path: Vercel — Gatsby outputs `public/`. With Gatsby Cloud sunset this is a real migration off, not a lateral move.
caveats: Gatsby Functions have to be ported to Vercel functions (similar shape).

wordpress.recommended_path: Don't try to run WordPress on Vercel. Vercel doesn't run PHP. Keep WordPress on its existing host (or a managed WP host like WP Engine / Kinsta) and put a CDN in front. If the front-end can be headless: build a Next.js front-end on Vercel that talks to WP REST/GraphQL.

laravel.recommended_path: PHP doesn't run on Vercel. Stay on Forge / a Laravel-friendly host (DigitalOcean, Fly, Railway, AWS) and front it with a CDN. If you want headless: Next.js on Vercel + Laravel API.

rails.recommended_path: Ruby/Rails doesn't run on Vercel. Use Fly, Railway, Render, or Heroku — they all have first-class Rails. If you want a JS front-end on Vercel that talks to Rails, that's fine.
caveats: ActionCable (WebSockets) is incompatible with Vercel even via API.

django.recommended_path: Python on Vercel works only as small per-file `api/` functions, not a full Django app. Keep Django on Fly/Railway/Render/AWS. Headless front-end on Vercel is fine.
caveats: Channels / WebSockets won't migrate.

flask.recommended_path: Tiny Flask APIs can ship to Vercel as a single Python serverless function (`api/index.py` exporting `app = Flask(__name__)`). Anything beyond a handful of routes — use Fly/Railway.
caveats: Cold starts for Python are heavier than Node.
Background tasks / Celery don't run on Vercel.

fastapi.recommended_path: Same shape as Flask. `api/index.py` exports the FastAPI app. Keep it small.

spring-boot.recommended_path: JVM doesn't run on Vercel. Use AWS / Azure / GCP / Fly. Vercel front-end + Spring Boot API on a JVM-friendly host is fine.

dotnet.recommended_path: ASP.NET / .NET doesn't run on Vercel. Azure App Service / AWS / Fly. Vercel front-end calling a .NET API works.

websocket-heavy.recommended_path: Vercel functions are short-lived; long-lived WebSocket connections don't fit. Use Fly Machines, Railway, or a dedicated realtime service (Pusher, Ably, Liveblocks). Vercel front-end can call them.

long-running-compute.recommended_path: Hobby caps at 10s, Pro 60s, Enterprise 15m max. Multi-minute / multi-hour compute → Fly / AWS / GCP / Modal / Inngest. Vercel can orchestrate but not host the compute.

heavy-database-app.recommended_path: Vercel functions can talk to any DB but every cold start adds connection-pool warm-up time. Use Vercel Postgres (Neon under the hood) for native pooling, or external + a serverless-friendly pooler (PgBouncer transaction mode, Neon, Supabase pooled).
caveats: Avoid TCP-only ORMs without a pooler — connection storms bring DBs down.

media-processing-heavy.recommended_path: FFmpeg / ImageMagick / headless Chrome at scale exceed function memory + timeout budgets. Use external workers (AWS Lambda + S3, Modal, Banana, Cloudflare R2 + Containers). Vercel's Image Optimization handles only image resize/format.

s3-storage.recommended_path: Stay on S3 (Vercel functions can talk to S3 directly), OR migrate to @vercel/blob if you want the storage-and-compute on the same provider. Blob is positioned for app-tier assets, not S3-feature-parity (no lifecycle, no Glacier).
caveats: S3 → Vercel Blob is one-way; plan a fallback path.
Compare egress: S3 has egress fees; Vercel Blob bandwidth is metered against the project.
